verses.text: Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls came and said to me, "Come, I will show you the punishment of the great prostitute, who sits on many waters.
The kings of the earth were immoral with her, and those who dwell on the earth were intoxicated with the wine of her immorality."
And the angel carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness, where I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet beast that was covered with blasphemous names and had seven heads and ten horns.
The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls. She held in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality.
And on her forehead a mysterious name was written: BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.
I could see that the woman was drunk with the blood of the saints and witnesses for Jesus. And I was utterly amazed at the sight of her.
"Why are you so amazed?" said the angel. "I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and ten horns.

The beast that you saw—it was, and now is no more, but is about to come up out of the Abyss and go to its destruction. And those who dwell on the earth whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see the beast that was, and is not, and yet will be.
This calls for a mind with wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits.
There are also seven kings. Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come; but when he does come, he must remain for only a little while.
The beast that was, and now is not, is an eighth king, who belongs to the other seven and is going into destruction.
The ten horns you saw are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom, but will receive one hour of authority as kings, along with the beast.
These kings have one purpose: to yield their power and authority to the beast.
They will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will triumph over them, because He is Lord of lords and King of kings; and He will be accompanied by His called and chosen and faithful ones."
Then the angel said to me, "The waters you saw, where the prostitute was seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.
And the ten horns and the beast that you saw will hate the prostitute. They will leave her desolate and naked, and will eat her flesh and burn her with fire.
For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose by uniting to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.
And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth."

context.author: John, who was on the island of Patmos (1:1, 4, 9); traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Apocalypse, prophecy, and letter, full of symbols and visions
context.audience: Seven churches in the Roman province of Asia
context.mapLabel: BABYLON, THE CITY ON SEVEN HILLS
context.setting: One of the bowl angels shows John the great prostitute seated on many waters, who sits on a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns. She is drunk with the blood of the saints and called “BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES” The angel explains that the seven heads are seven hills and also seven kings.
context.custom: Rome was well known as the city on seven hills. Prophets used the image of a prostitute for cities and nations that traded in power and idolatry (Nahum 3:4; Isaiah 23:16-17). Roman coins show the goddess Roma seated on seven hills.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 18 describes Babylon’s fall and the mourning of kings and merchants.
context.timelineBible: Babylon, Tyre, and Nineveh in the prophets lie behind this picture (Isaiah 13, 23; Jeremiah 50-51; Ezekiel 26-27). “Many waters” echoes Jeremiah 51:13.

translation.meaning: A symbolic secret meaning, which the angel then explains.
A prophetic picture of idolatrous unfaithfulness.

otBackground.note: Nineveh, the prostitute with her charms.
Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord’s hand.

overview.summary: The prostitute Babylon rides the beast and is drunk with the blood of the saints. The angel explains the vision, and the Lamb will conquer.
overview.settingLine: A vision of Babylon the great.

history.t: Rome was proverbial as the city of seven hills.
Seven kings may correspond to a series of emperors.

customs.t: A cup of wine in a pagan rite.

archaeology.t: Coins from Vespasian show Roma seated on seven hills.
Coins of Nero, Vespasian and Domitian show how the emperors presented themselves as divine or near-divine, part of the background to the beast and the woman who rides it.

overview.discussion: John’s vision exposes a seductive power that rides on wealth and violence. What attractive things in my world might blind me to hidden costs?
overview.book: The book of Revelation · 22 chapters. A vision of Christ, judgment, and the new creation, written to encourage persecuted believers.
overview.author: John

currentImage.caption: A portrait of the emperor Nero (ruled AD 54-68) in the Capitoline Museums, Rome, restored in the 17th century. Nero persecuted the Christians of Rome in AD 64. The numbers 666 and 616 both fit his name written in Hebrew letters, and rumors after his death said he would return.
